relationship: Changing the seed environment changes differential reproduction of existing inherited beak variation, so trait frequencies change across generations rather than individual birds changing their beaks.

learnerLoop.action: Move food advantage, select parents, replace adults with their offspring, and sustain three different pressures.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Environment changes reproductive weights of existing adults. Weighted parent selection and inherited variation generate a new fixed-size population.
learnerLoop.evidence: Large bird glyphs illustrate three representative beak depths; count dots and frequency bars derive from the same population as mean, spread and middle-band readings. Original adults remain in place when food is edited.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Compare directional, stabilising and disruptive effects, then reverse or reshape food in the experiment.

invariants: Editing the environment changes likely parents without changing existing adult traits.
Selection precedes inheritance and generation replacement; offspring resemble successful parents with variation.
Distribution and numerical evidence describe the same population and distinguish the three selection patterns.
safeAdaptations: Change organism context or guidance while preserving heritable variation and differential reproduction.
Offer additional seed environments and prediction prompts that test changes in frequency over generations.
nonGoals: Do not portray adaptation as individuals deliberately acquiring a needed trait.
Do not extend this population model into a full genetic or ecological simulator.

prompt.description: A visually identified current mission, with context connecting the previous experience to the next action.

model.description: Environment changes reproductive weights of existing adults. Weighted parent selection and inherited variation generate a new fixed-size population.
model.visibility: Always visible; later controls are progressively disclosed.

working.description: Worked examples precede learner calculations. Explicit quantity keys connect source labels to formula operands, with sequential animation, matching highlights and replay. Hover, focus and tap explain each source and calculation.

evidence.description: Large bird glyphs illustrate three representative beak depths; count dots and frequency bars derive from the same population as mean, spread and middle-band readings. Original adults remain in place when food is edited.
evidence.visibility: In-place feedback; readings only in relevant steps.

completion.description: Advances only after the current model-derived criterion.
completion.visibility: Guided steps; absent in the open experiment.

food.description: One or two Gaussian food-advantage peaks across the beak-depth axis.
food.domain: Peak centres 4.5 to 15.5 mm; widths 0.55 to 3 mm.
food.source: SVG food-peak and independent food-width handles.
food.output: Reproductive weights; no direct adult trait change.

population.description: Inherited beak-depth values for every adult.
population.domain: 4.05 to 15.95 mm; 72 adults and 24 parents guided. Experiment populations of 36, 72 or 144, with one third selected as parents.
population.source: Seeded weighted sampling with offspring variation of SD 0.43 mm.
population.output: Adult count dots, parent-to-offspring transitions, beak-depth frequency bars and mean/SD/middle frequencies.

frequency.description: Percentage of the current adults within a named trait group.
frequency.domain: 0 to 100 percent; the assessed middle group is 8.5–11.5 mm inclusive.
frequency.source: Group adult count divided by the total population and multiplied by 100; guided total 72.
frequency.output: Worked frequency examples precede a checked learner calculation to one decimal place.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Ungated experiment: one/two movable peaks with independent widths, steady/alternating/even food, populations of 36/72/144, inherited reproduction and history.

dependencies: Move food advantage toward deeper existing beaks.
Select 24 parents, observe 72 offspring inheriting traits from those parents, then replace the adults after the transition.
At least three generations and mean rise above 1.2 mm.
At least three generations, SD below 78% of baseline, and a checked middle-group frequency within 0.11 percentage points.
At least four generations, wider SD, smaller middle, and at least 15% in each tail.
Ungated experiment: one/two movable peaks with independent widths, steady/alternating/even food, populations of 36/72/144, inherited reproduction and history.
implementation.completion: Every guided criterion is evaluated from actual model state. Continue never bypasses an unmet criterion. Restart returns to the first step; Back repeats a prior step.
limitations: Simplified heritable continuous trait, not a complete genetic, ecological, or demographic simulation.

Population size stays fixed within a run. Choosing a size starts a fresh seeded cohort. Steady food is editable; alternating food switches shallow/deep advantage after each generation; even food gives all traits equal reproductive weights, while random sampling remains.
Dashed columns show starting frequencies; bars show every current adult. Bird drawings are representative trait examples. Spread is population standard deviation; the middle band is 8.5–11.5 mm.
